Hi Samantha / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really useful call. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary concern: protecting customer PII and ensuring strict access controls for production data.
- Data residency: production workload needs to remain in us-east-1.
- Logging & retention: audit logs for support access and admin actions are required; you indicated a 30-day hot log retention with the ability to export longer-term records for compliance.
- Support access: break-glass flow required with documented approvals and full audit trail.
- RBAC: least-privilege roles for both internal staff and any third-party/partner integrations.

What we committed to provide
1) SOC 2 summary and short list of relevant controls (we'll attach an executive summary).
2) A short diagram and note on how Redwood implements RBAC, support access, and break-glass (I'll loop in our SE).
3) Confirmation on data residency options and how we pin deployment regions.
4) Proposed technical deep-dive (30-45m) with our SE and CS to walk the support access flow and logging retention.

Proposed next steps
- I'll share the SOC2 summary + access-controls diagram by EOD tomorrow (attached).
- Can we schedule the deep-dive next week? I have availability Tue/Wed afternoon PST.
- Samantha: if you can share any internal checklist or minimum bar items for support access that would help us tailor the demo.

Thanks,

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@fintrust.com>

Date: 2027-08-31T18:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Access controls & data handling - FinTrust / Redwood

Thanks Marissa — great recap and yes, that aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and asks from our security team: 

- RBAC & least privilege: We need role separation (admin, support-engineer, auditor) and the ability to scope access to specific customer accounts.
- Support access / break-glass: Must be time-bound, require an approval workflow (manager + security), and record the justification. All activity performed during break-glass must be logged and retained.
- Logging retention: 30 days hot for quick search; for compliance we need exports / archived logs retained for 7 years for any PII access events.
- Data residency: Production data must reside in us-east-1. Backups can be multi-region only if encrypted and access-restricted; we prefer single-region.
- Authentication: SSO (SAML) + MFA required for all Redwood user access to our account.

Artifacts we need to see: SOC 2 Type II report (or summary), pen-test summary, and a description of your break-glass approval workflow. If you can provide those prior to the technical deep-dive, that would be ideal.

We can target Tue Sep 7 or Wed Sep 8 for the deep-dive — Tue afternoon ET works best for our team.

Thanks,
Samantha
Director, InfoSec | FinTrust
samantha.lee@fintrust.com
